title: Automate Infrastructure Provisioning via ARM Templates & CLI
summary: Deploy parameterized Azure infrastructure declaratively using Azure Resource Manager (ARM) JSON templates, Azure CLI, and PowerShell.
scenarioTemplate: You are a Cloud Administrator at {{companyName}}. Your organization is establishing standardized, declarative infrastructure deployments for new workloads in '{{region}}'. You are tasked with creating a target resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' and executing a parameterized ARM template deployment named '{{deploymentName}}' to provision a General-purpose v2 storage account named '{{storageAccount}}' with standard LRS redundancy and strict HTTPS enforcement.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Author an ARM template JSON file (template.json) defining a Standard_LRS StorageV2 account.
Execute declarative template deployment '{{deploymentName}}' against '{{resourceGroup}}' using Azure CLI or PowerShell.
Verify the template deployment succeeded by inspecting deployment operations and resource provisioningState.

steps.title: Create the Target Resource Group
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal search bar, type **Resource groups** > **+ Create**. Choose your subscription, name the resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`, and set Region to `{{region}}`. Click **Review + create** > **Create**.

steps.title: Author Parameterized ARM Template
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal, open **Cloud Shell** (Bash or PowerShell). Generate the local template file `template.json` specifying schema, parameters, and storage resources.

steps.title: Validate and Deploy the ARM Template
steps.portalGuide: In the portal search bar, search for **Deploy a custom template** > **Build your own template in the editor**. Paste the JSON schema > **Save**. Set Resource group to `{{resourceGroup}}`, `storageName` to `{{storageAccount}}`, `location` to `{{region}}` > Click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Preflight validation:
az deployment group validate \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --template-file template.json \
  --parameters storageName={{storageAccount}} location={{region}}

# Execute deployment:
az deployment group create \
  --name {{deploymentName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --template-file template.json \
  --parameters storageName={{storageAccount}} location={{region}}
steps.powershellCommand:
# Preflight validation:
Test-AzResourceGroupDeployment -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -TemplateFile template.json -storageName '{{storageAccount}}' -location '{{region}}'

# Execute deployment:
New-AzResourceGroupDeployment -Name '{{deploymentName}}' -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -TemplateFile template.json -storageName '{{storageAccount}}' -location '{{region}}'

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: Navigate to **Resource groups** > find `{{resourceGroup}}` > click **Delete resource group** > type the name to confirm > click **Delete**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
rm -f template.json

title: Enforce Resource Tagging and Resource Locks for Governance
summary: Standardize resource metadata using Azure Tags and apply management locks to prevent accidental deletion of critical infrastructure.
scenarioTemplate: Enterprise governance policy at {{companyName}} mandates that all resources deployed for accounting and workload tracking must bear required tags: Environment = '{{environmentTag}}', CostCenter = '{{costCenter}}', and Owner = '{{ownerName}}'. In resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provision a storage account '{{storageAccount}}', enforce the metadata tags, and attach a '{{lockType}}' management lock named '{{lockName}}' to guarantee administrators cannot delete the resource group accidentally.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Apply tags Environment='{{environmentTag}}', CostCenter='{{costCenter}}', and Owner='{{ownerName}}' to '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Create standard storage account '{{storageAccount}}' inside '{{resourceGroup}}' and inherit/apply the tags.
Apply a '{{lockType}}' resource lock named '{{lockName}}' to '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Test deleting the resource group to verify the lock blocks deletion with an error, then remove the lock and clean up.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Apply Tags
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Resource groups** > **+ Create**. Name: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Click **Next: Tags**. Add `Environment` = `{{environmentTag}}`, `CostCenter` = `{{costCenter}}`, `Owner` = `{{ownerName}}`. Click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create \
  --name {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --tags Environment={{environmentTag}} CostCenter={{costCenter}} Owner={{ownerName}}

steps.title: Deploy Storage Account with Matching Tags
steps.portalGuide: Open `{{resourceGroup}}` > **+ Create** > **Storage account**. Name: `{{storageAccount}}`, Standard LRS. Under **Tags**, apply matching `Environment` = `{{environmentTag}}` and `CostCenter` = `{{costCenter}}` tags. Click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
az storage account create \
  --name {{storageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2 \
  --tags Environment={{environmentTag}} CostCenter={{costCenter}} Owner={{ownerName}}
steps.validation: az resource list --tag CostCenter={{costCenter}} --query "[].{Name:name, Type:type, Tags:tags}" -o table

steps.title: Configure Resource Lock on Resource Group
steps.portalGuide: Navigate to resource group `{{resourceGroup}}` > select **Locks** in the left blade > **+ Add**. Lock name: `{{lockName}}`, Lock type: `{{lockType}}`, Notes: `Mandatory protection policy`. Click **OK**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group lock create \
  --name {{lockName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --lock-type {{lockType}} \
  --notes "Mandatory governance lock for {{companyName}}"
steps.validation: az group lock list --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query "[].{Name:name, Level:level}" -o table

steps.title: Verify Lock Enforcement and Clean Up
steps.portalGuide: Try deleting the resource group: click **Delete resource group** > confirm name > click **Delete**. Notice the portal blocks the operation indicating a lock is active. Remove the lock from the **Locks** blade, then delete the resource group.
steps.cliCommand:
# 1. Test deletion fails due to lock:
az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes || echo "Expected: Locked resource prevented deletion!"

# 2. Delete lock:
az group lock delete --name {{lockName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}}

# 3. Clean up:
az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
steps.powershellCommand:
# 1. Delete lock:
Remove-AzResourceLock -LockName '{{lockName}}' -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Force

# 2. Clean up:
Remove-AzResourceGroup -Name '{{resourceGroup}}' -Force

title: Manage Microsoft Entra ID Users, Security Groups, and SSPR
summary: Create cloud user identities, configure organizational properties, organize into security groups, and enable Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR).
scenarioTemplate: You are the Lead Identity Administrator for {{companyName}}. As part of onboarding a new department ('{{department}}'), you must provision a member user account ('{{userName}}'), assign their usage location to '{{usageLocation}}', create a security group named '{{groupName}}', add the user to the group, and configure Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) authentication methods.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a Microsoft Entra ID user account with User Principal Name '{{userName}}@<your-tenant>.onmicrosoft.com'.
Set Job Title to '{{jobTitle}}', Department to '{{department}}', and Usage Location to '{{usageLocation}}'.
Create a Microsoft Entra Security Group named '{{groupName}}' with Assigned membership.
Add user '{{userName}}' as a member of '{{groupName}}'.
Verify group membership and inspect Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) configuration.

steps.title: Create User Account with Organizational Attributes
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal, open **Microsoft Entra ID** > select **Users** in the left blade > click **+ New user** > **Create new user**. Set User principal name to `{{userName}}`, Display name to `{{displayName}}`. Under **Properties**, set Job Title to `{{jobTitle}}`, Department to `{{department}}`, and Usage Location to `{{usageLocation}}`. Set an initial password > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Retrieve default tenant domain:
DOMAIN=$(az rest --method get --url "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/domains" --query 'value[?isDefault].id' -o tsv)

# Create user:
az ad user create \
  --display-name "{{displayName}}" \
  --user-principal-name "{{userName}}@$DOMAIN" \
  --password "Pass@word12345!" \
  --force-change-password-next-sign-in false
steps.validation: az ad user show --id "{{userName}}@$(az rest --method get --url 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/domains' --query 'value[?isDefault].id' -o tsv)" --query '{Name:displayName, Dept:department, Title:jobTitle}' -o table

steps.title: Create Security Group and Add User Member
steps.portalGuide: In **Microsoft Entra ID**, select **Groups** > click **+ New group**. Group type: **Security**, Group name: `{{groupName}}`, Group description: `Pilot group for {{department}}`, Membership type: **Assigned**. Click **No members selected** > search for `{{displayName}}` > select user > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Create group:
az ad group create \
  --display-name "{{groupName}}" \
  --mail-nickname "{{groupName}}"

# Add user to group:
USER_ID=$(az ad user show --id "{{userName}}@$(az rest --method get --url 'https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/domains' --query 'value[?isDefault].id' -o tsv)" --query id -o tsv)
az ad group member add --group "{{groupName}}" --member-id "$USER_ID"
steps.validation: az ad group member list --group "{{groupName}}" --query "[].{Name:displayName, Type:principalType}" -o table

steps.title: Inspect Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) Settings
steps.portalGuide: In **Microsoft Entra ID**, scroll down to **Password reset** in the manage menu. Under **Manage** > **Properties**, review Self service password reset enabled: select **Selected** > pick `{{groupName}}` to scope SSPR to this group. Under **Authentication methods**, note that 1 or 2 methods can be required (Mobile app, Email, Phone) > click **Save**.
steps.cliCommand:
# Check tenant-wide authentication methods policy via Graph:
az rest --method get --url "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy" --query 'id' -o tsv

steps.title: Clean Up Identity Resources
steps.portalGuide: In **Microsoft Entra ID** > **Groups** > delete `{{groupName}}`. Go to **Users** > select `{{displayName}}` > click **Delete user**.
steps.cliCommand:
DOMAIN=$(az rest --method get --url "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/domains" --query 'value[?isDefault].id' -o tsv)
az ad group delete --group "{{groupName}}"
az ad user delete --id "{{userName}}@$DOMAIN"

title: Configure Scoped Azure RBAC Role Assignments
summary: Create a resource group, provision target infrastructure, and delegate least-privilege role-based access control to a security group without exposing account access keys.
scenarioTemplate: You are an Azure Administrator for {{companyName}}. An engineering team (represented by security group '{{groupName}}') requires access to manage resources in the '{{region}}' region. In accordance with enterprise Zero Trust and least-privilege compliance, you must assign the '{{targetRole.name}}' role scoped strictly to the '{{resourceGroup}}' resource group (or specific resource). Account shared keys must not be shared.

targetRole.name: Storage Blob Data Contributor
targetRole.description: Grants read, write, and delete permissions to Azure Storage blob containers and data.

targetRole.name: Storage Blob Data Reader
targetRole.description: Grants read and list permissions to Azure Storage containers and blobs.

targetRole.name: Storage Account Contributor
targetRole.description: Grants management permissions over the storage account resource, but cannot read data plane blobs directly without listKeys.

targetRole.name: Reader
targetRole.description: View all resources, but does not allow making any changes.

acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in location '{{region}}'.
Deploy a standard general-purpose v2 storage account named '{{storageAccount}}' with LRS redundancy.
Identify or create a Microsoft Entra security group named '{{groupName}}'.
Assign the built-in role '{{targetRole.name}}' to group '{{groupName}}' scoped to '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Verify that the role assignment exists and inspect its assignment ID.

steps.title: Create the Resource Group and Storage Account
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal search bar, type **Resource groups** and select **+ Create**. Set Name to `{{resourceGroup}}` and Region to `{{region}}`. Once created, search for **Storage accounts** > **+ Create**. Place it in `{{resourceGroup}}`, name it `{{storageAccount}}`, set Performance to Standard, and Redundancy to Locally-redundant storage (LRS).
steps.cliCommand:
az group create \
  --name {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}}

az storage account create \
  --name {{storageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

steps.title: Create or Retrieve the Microsoft Entra Security Group
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal, open **Microsoft Entra ID** > **Groups** > **New group**. Select Group type: **Security**, Group name: `{{groupName}}`, and click **Create**. Click into the group and copy the **Object ID**.
steps.cliCommand:
az ad group create \
  --display-name "{{groupName}}" \
  --mail-nickname "{{groupName}}"

# Retrieve Group Object ID:
GROUP_ID=$(az ad group show --group "{{groupName}}" --query id -o tsv)
echo "Group Object ID: $GROUP_ID"

steps.title: Assign the Role Scoped to the Resource Group
steps.portalGuide: Open resource group `{{resourceGroup}}` > click **Access control (IAM)** > **+ Add** > **Add role assignment**. Select Role: `{{targetRole.name}}` > Next. Assign access to: **User, group, or service principal** > click **+ Select members** > search for `{{groupName}}` > select it > Review + assign.
steps.cliCommand:
GROUP_ID=$(az ad group show --group "{{groupName}}" --query id -o tsv)
RG_ID=$(az group show --name {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

az role assignment create \
  --role "{{targetRole.name}}" \
  --assignee-object-id "$GROUP_ID" \
  --assignee-principal-type Group \
  --scope "$RG_ID"
steps.validation: az role assignment list --scope /subscriptions/$(az account show --query id -o tsv)/resourceGroups/{{resourceGroup}} --query "[?roleDefinitionName=='{{targetRole.name}}'].{Principal:principalName, Role:roleDefinitionName}" -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Lab Resources
steps.portalGuide: To avoid recurring charges, navigate to **Resource groups** > find `{{resourceGroup}}` > click **Delete resource group** > type the name to confirm > click **Delete**.
steps.cliCommand:
az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
az ad group delete --group "{{groupName}}"

title: Author and Deploy Granular Custom Azure RBAC Roles
summary: Author a custom RBAC JSON definition with explicit Actions, NotActions, and AssignableScopes to enforce least-privilege VM management.
scenarioTemplate: Security operations at {{companyName}} requires a specialized role named '{{customRoleName}}' for operations staff in resource group '{{resourceGroup}}'. Members must be permitted to start, restart, and inspect virtual machines and read network interfaces, but must explicitly NOT be allowed to delete virtual machines or modify disks. You must author a custom role JSON definition and register it at your subscription scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Retrieve current Azure subscription ID to use in AssignableScopes.
Author a custom role JSON file (custom-role.json) granting VM start, restart, read, and NIC read, with explicit delete NotActions.
Register the custom role definition using Azure CLI or PowerShell.
Verify the custom role is available in the tenant, and clean up afterwards.

steps.title: Retrieve Subscription ID and Create Resource Group
steps.portalGuide: Open the Azure Portal > search for **Subscriptions** and copy your **Subscription ID**. Search for **Resource groups** > **+ Create** > Name: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Region: `{{region}}`.

steps.title: Author Custom Role JSON Definition
steps.portalGuide: In Azure Cloud Shell, create a file named `custom-role.json` specifying the required `Actions`, `NotActions`, and `AssignableScopes` targeting your subscription.
steps.cliCommand:
SUB_ID=$(az account show --query id -o tsv)
cat << EOF > custom-role.json
{
  "Name": "{{customRoleName}}",
  "IsDataAction": false,
  "Description": "Allows starting, restarting, and reading VMs, but strictly denies deletion.",
  "Actions": [
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read",
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action",
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/restart/action",
    "Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces/read"
  ],
  "NotActions": [
    "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete"
  ],
  "DataActions": [],
  "NotDataActions": [],
  "AssignableScopes": [
    "/subscriptions/$SUB_ID"
  ]
}
EOF
steps.powershellCommand:
$subId = (Get-AzContext).Subscription.Id
@"
{
  `"Name`": `"{{customRoleName}}`",
  `"IsDataAction`": false,
  `"Description`": `"Allows starting, restarting, and reading VMs, but strictly denies deletion.`",
  `"Actions`": [
    `"Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read`",
    `"Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action`",
    `"Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/restart/action`",
    `"Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces/read`"
  ],
  `"NotActions`": [
    `"Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete`"
  ],
  `"AssignableScopes`": [
    `"/subscriptions/$subId`"
  ]
}
"@ | Out-File -FilePath custom-role.json -Encoding utf8

steps.title: Create and Register the Custom Role
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal, open **Subscriptions** > your subscription > **Access control (IAM)** > **+ Add** > **Add custom role**. Choose **Start from JSON** > upload `custom-role.json` > review actions > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand: az role definition create --role-definition custom-role.json
steps.validation: az role definition list --name "{{customRoleName}}" --query "[].{Name:roleName, Type:roleType, Description:description}" -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Custom Role and Resource Group
steps.portalGuide: In Subscriptions > Access control (IAM) > **Roles** > search for `{{customRoleName}}` > click `...` > **Delete**. Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
az role definition delete --name "{{customRoleName}}"
az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
rm -f custom-role.json

title: Enforce Compliance with Azure Policy Definitions and Initiatives
summary: Implement organizational guardrails by assigning Azure Policy definitions to prevent unauthorized regions and missing tags.
scenarioTemplate: Corporate data residency requirements at {{companyName}} dictate that workloads in resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' may only be provisioned in approved regions ('{{allowedRegion}}'). To prevent compliance violations, assign the built-in 'Allowed locations' policy scoped to '{{resourceGroup}}'. Test the policy by attempting to deploy a storage account in a non-compliant region ('{{deniedRegion}}') to verify that Azure Resource Manager blocks the deployment.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in allowed location '{{allowedRegion}}'.
Assign the built-in Azure Policy 'Allowed locations' scoped to '{{resourceGroup}}' with allowedValues set to ['{{allowedRegion}}'].
Attempt to deploy a storage account in denied region '{{deniedRegion}}' and verify RequestDisallowedByPolicy error.
Successfully deploy a storage account in allowed region '{{allowedRegion}}' to verify compliance.
Remove the policy assignment and clean up lab resources.

steps.title: Create Target Resource Group
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Resource groups** > **+ Create**. Name: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Region: `{{allowedRegion}}`. Click **Review + create** > **Create**.

steps.title: Assign Allowed Locations Policy Definition
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal search bar, type **Policy**. In the left menu, select **Assignments** > **Assign policy**. Scope: `{{resourceGroup}}`. Policy definition: search for **Allowed locations** (Built-in) > select it. Under **Parameters**, select `{{allowedRegion}}`. Assignment name: `{{policyAssignmentName}}`. Click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
RG_ID=$(az group show --name {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

az policy assignment create \
  --name {{policyAssignmentName}} \
  --scope "$RG_ID" \
  --policy "e56962a6-4747-49cd-b67b-bf7b01975c4c" \
  --params "{\"listOfAllowedLocations\": {\"value\": [\"{{allowedRegion}}\"]}}"
steps.validation: az policy assignment show --name {{policyAssignmentName}} --scope $(az group show --name {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv) --query '{Name:name, Scope:scope}' -o table

steps.title: Test Policy Block and Compliance
steps.portalGuide: Try creating a storage account in `{{resourceGroup}}` with location set to `{{deniedRegion}}`. The portal validation step will report an error: `Validation failed. Required by policy {{policyAssignmentName}}`. Then change location to `{{allowedRegion}}` and observe validation passes.
steps.cliCommand:
# 1. Test DENIED deployment (Expected to FAIL with RequestDisallowedByPolicy):
az storage account create \
  --name {{testStorageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{deniedRegion}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS || echo "[Expected] Blocked by Azure Policy!"

# 2. Test ALLOWED deployment:
az storage account create \
  --name {{testStorageAccount}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{allowedRegion}} \
  --sku Standard_LRS
steps.powershellCommand:
# Test creation in allowed region:
New-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name '{{testStorageAccount}}' -Location '{{allowedRegion}}' -SkuName 'Standard_LRS' -Kind 'StorageV2'

steps.title: Delete Policy Assignment and Clean Up
steps.portalGuide: In **Policy** > **Assignments** > find `{{policyAssignmentName}}` > click `...` > **Delete assignment**. Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
RG_ID=$(az group show --name {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)
az policy assignment delete --name {{policyAssignmentName}} --scope "$RG_ID"
az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait

title: Configure Management Groups and Azure Cost Management Budgets
summary: Organize cloud subscriptions into hierarchical Management Groups and configure automated cost alerts and budgets.
scenarioTemplate: As FinOps Administrator at {{companyName}}, you are tasked with structuring organizational governance. You must create a new Management Group named '{{mgmtGroupName}}', organize resource groups under financial monitoring, and establish a monthly budget of ${{budgetAmount}} in Azure Cost Management with automated email threshold alerts (50%, 80%, and 100%) to '{{contactEmail}}'.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a Microsoft Entra-linked Management Group named '{{mgmtGroupName}}'.
Inspect management group hierarchy and root group associations.
Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' for workload cost tracking.
Configure an Azure Cost Management budget named '{{budgetName}}' with amount ${{budgetAmount}}.
Set up notification alert rules at 50%, 80%, and 100% threshold percentages directed to '{{contactEmail}}'.

steps.title: Create Management Group Hierarchy
steps.portalGuide: In the Azure Portal search bar, type **Management groups**. Click **+ Create**. Set Management group ID and display name to `{{mgmtGroupName}}` > click **Submit**.
steps.cliCommand:
az account management-group create \
  --name "{{mgmtGroupName}}" \
  --display-name "{{mgmtGroupName}}"
steps.validation: az account management-group show --name "{{mgmtGroupName}}" --query '{ID:name, Display:displayName}' -o table

steps.title: Create Workload Resource Group for Scoped Budgeting
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Resource groups** > **+ Create**. Name: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Region: `eastus` > click **Review + create** > **Create**.
steps.cliCommand: az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location eastus

steps.title: Configure Cost Management Budget and Threshold Alerts
steps.portalGuide: Navigate to `{{resourceGroup}}` > in the left menu, select **Budgets** (under Cost Management) > **+ Add**. Name: `{{budgetName}}`, Reset period: **Monthly**, Creation date: Today, Expiration date: 2 years out, Amount: `{{budgetAmount}}`. Click **Next**. Alert condition 1: Type **Actual**, % of budget: `50`, Email recipients: `{{contactEmail}}`. Add condition 2: `80`%, condition 3: `100`%. Click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
START_DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-01)
END_DATE=$(date -d "+2 years" +%Y-%m-01 2>/dev/null || date -v+2y +%Y-%m-01)

az consumption budget create \
  --budget-name {{budgetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --amount {{budgetAmount}} \
  --time-grain monthly \
  --start-date $START_DATE \
  --end-date $END_DATE
steps.validation: az consumption budget show --budget-name {{budgetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Budget:name, Amount:amount, TimeGrain:timeGrain}' -o table

steps.title: Clean Up Management Group and Budget
steps.portalGuide: In `{{resourceGroup}}` > **Budgets** > select `{{budgetName}}` > click **Delete**. Delete resource group `{{resourceGroup}}`. In **Management groups**, select `{{mgmtGroupName}}` > click **Delete**.
steps.cliCommand:
az consumption budget delete --budget-name {{budgetName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --yes
az group delete --name {{resourceGroup}} --yes --no-wait
az account management-group delete --name "{{mgmtGroupName}}"
steps.validation: echo "Budget and management group cleanup complete."

title: Secure Multi-Tier Virtual Network with Subnets and NSGs
summary: Architect a segmented virtual network with web and database subnets, then enforce traffic isolation using Network Security Groups (NSGs) and Application Security Groups (ASGs).
scenarioTemplate: You are designing network infrastructure for an application in '{{region}}'. You must deploy a Virtual Network named '{{vnetName}}' with address space '{{vnetPrefix}}'. Inside, create two subnets: a web tier subnet ('{{webSubnetName}}', {{webSubnetPrefix}}) and a database tier subnet ('{{dbSubnetName}}', {{dbSubnetPrefix}}). Configure an NSG named '{{nsgName}}' to allow inbound port {{webPort}} to the web tier, while completely blocking the database tier from direct public Internet exposure.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Create Virtual Network '{{vnetName}}' with CIDR '{{vnetPrefix}}'.
Add frontend subnet '{{webSubnetName}}' ({{webSubnetPrefix}}) and backend subnet '{{dbSubnetName}}' ({{dbSubnetPrefix}}).
Create Network Security Group '{{nsgName}}' with an Inbound rule allowing TCP port {{webPort}} with priority 200.
Associate '{{nsgName}}' to subnet '{{webSubnetName}}'.
Verify effective NSG associations on the subnet.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Segmented Virtual Network
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Virtual networks** > **+ Create**. Resource group: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{vnetName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Under **IP addresses**, set address space to `{{vnetPrefix}}`. Add subnet `{{webSubnetName}}` with range `{{webSubnetPrefix}}`, then add subnet `{{dbSubnetName}}` with range `{{dbSubnetPrefix}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az network vnet create \
  --name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --address-prefixes {{vnetPrefix}} \
  --subnet-name {{webSubnetName}} \
  --subnet-prefixes {{webSubnetPrefix}}

az network vnet subnet create \
  --name {{dbSubnetName}} \
  --vnet-name {{vnetName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --address-prefixes {{dbSubnetPrefix}}
steps.validation: az network vnet subnet list --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --vnet-name {{vnetName}} -o table

steps.title: Create Network Security Group and Inbound Port Rule
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Network security groups** > **+ Create**. Select RG `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{nsgName}}`, Region: `{{region}}`. Once deployed, open the NSG > **Inbound security rules** > **+ Add**. Source: Any, Destination: Any, Destination port: `{{webPort}}`, Protocol: TCP, Action: Allow, Priority: 200, Name: `Allow_Web_{{webPort}}`.
steps.cliCommand:
az network nsg create \
  --name {{nsgName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}}

az network nsg rule create \
  --name Allow_Web_{{webPort}} \
  --nsg-name {{nsgName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --priority 200 \
  --access Allow \
  --direction Inbound \
  --protocol Tcp \
  --destination-port-ranges {{webPort}}

title: Configure Azure Monitor Log Analytics Workspaces and Diagnostic Settings

You are tasked with creating resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', provisioning an Azure Log Analytics Workspace named '{{workspaceName}}' with a {{retentionDays}}-day data retention period, configuring Diagnostic Settings on a target resource to export logs and metrics, and executing sample Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Log Analytics Workspace

title: Configure Azure Metric Alerts and Multi-Channel Action Groups
summary: Implement proactive incident notification by configuring Action Groups and Azure Metric Alert rules with static evaluation thresholds.
scenarioTemplate: You are establishing operational alert notifications for production workloads in '{{region}}'. Inside resource group '{{resourceGroup}}', create an Action Group named '{{actionGroupName}}' configured to send email notifications to '{{emailAddress}}'. Then create an Azure Metric Alert rule named '{{alertRuleName}}' that evaluates every 5 minutes and fires a Severity {{severity}} alert when average CPU percentage (or storage capacity) exceeds {{thresholdPct}}%.
acceptanceCriteria: Create resource group '{{resourceGroup}}' in '{{region}}'.
Create an Action Group named '{{actionGroupName}}' with short name '{{shortName}}' and an Email receiver pointing to '{{emailAddress}}'.
Deploy a target Virtual Machine or App Service resource to monitor.
Create a Metric Alert rule named '{{alertRuleName}}' targeting the resource with condition 'Percentage CPU > {{thresholdPct}}'.
Attach '{{actionGroupName}}' to the alert rule with Severity {{severity}}.
Verify the alert rule status is enabled and inspect notification configuration.

steps.title: Create Resource Group and Action Group
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Monitor** > in the left menu, select **Alerts** > click **Action groups** > **+ Create**. RG: `{{resourceGroup}}`, Name: `{{actionGroupName}}`, Display name: `{{shortName}}`. steps.title: Deploy Test Compute Resource
steps.portalGuide: Deploy a lightweight VM `vm-alert-test` in `{{resourceGroup}}` (Ubuntu2204, Standard_B1s) to serve as the metric alert target.
steps.cliCommand:
az vm create \
  --name vm-alert-test \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size Standard_B1s \
  --generate-ssh-keys

steps.title: Create Metric Alert Rule Linked to Action Group
steps.portalGuide: In **Monitor** > **Alerts** > click **+ Create** > **Alert rule**. Scope: select `vm-alert-test`. Condition: Signal name **Percentage CPU**, Operator: **Greater than**, Threshold: `{{thresholdPct}}`, Check every: `5 minutes`. Actions: Select existing action group `{{actionGroupName}}`. Details: Severity **{{severity}} - Warning**, Alert rule name: `{{alertRuleName}}` > click **Create**.
steps.cliCommand:
VM_ID=$(az vm show --name vm-alert-test --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)
AG_ID=$(az monitor action-group show --name {{actionGroupName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query id -o tsv)

az monitor metrics alert create \
  --name {{alertRuleName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --scopes "$VM_ID" \
  --condition "avg Percentage CPU > {{thresholdPct}}" \
  --window-size 5m \
  --evaluation-frequency 1m \
  --action "$AG_ID" \
  --severity {{severity}} \
  --description "Alert when CPU spikes above {{thresholdPct}}%"
steps.powershellCommand:
$vm = Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name 'vm-alert-test'
$ag = Get-AzActionGroup -ResourceGroupName '{{resourceGroup}}' -Name '{{actionGroupName}}'
# Metric alert creation via PowerShell or Azure CLI
az monitor metrics alert show --name {{alertRuleName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}}
steps.validation: az monitor metrics alert show --name {{alertRuleName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query '{Name:name, Severity:severity, Enabled:enabled}' -o table

title: Troubleshoot Network Connectivity using Azure Network Watcher
summary: Diagnose network connectivity issues, verify NSG traffic filtering using IP Flow Verify, and inspect routing with Next Hop analysis.

You must utilize Azure Network Watcher in '{{region}}' to diagnose the failure. Using **IP Flow Verify**, determine whether inbound or outbound NSG security rules are dropping packets. Then run **Next Hop** analysis on Virtual Machine '{{vmName}}' to confirm whether traffic routes via VirtualAppliance, VirtualNetwork, or Internet.
acceptanceCriteria: Verify Azure Network Watcher is enabled for region '{{region}}'.
Deploy Virtual Machine '{{vmName}}' in '{{resourceGroup}}'.
Execute Network Watcher IP Flow Verify test on '{{vmName}}' targeting IP '{{targetIp}}' on port {{targetPort}}.
Execute Network Watcher Next Hop analysis from '{{vmName}}' to target IP '{{targetIp}}'.
Interpret results (Access Allowed / Denied and effective security rule name).
Clean up all lab resources.

steps.title: Verify Network Watcher and Create Test VM
steps.portalGuide: Search for **Network Watcher**. Verify your target region `{{region}}` status is **Enabled**. Create RG `{{resourceGroup}}` and deploy VM `{{vmName}}` (Ubuntu2204, Standard_B1s) with a virtual network.
steps.cliCommand:
# Ensure Network Watcher is enabled for region:
az network watcher configure \
  --locations {{region}} \
  --enabled true \
  --resource-group NetworkWatcherRG 2>/dev/null || true

az group create --name {{resourceGroup}} --location {{region}}

az vm create \
  --name {{vmName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --location {{region}} \
  --image Ubuntu2204 \
  --size Standard_B1s \
  --generate-ssh-keys
steps.validation: az network watcher list --query "[?location=='{{region}}'].{Location:location, Provisioning:provisioningState}" -o table

steps.title: Run IP Flow Verify to Inspect NSG Rule Evaluation
steps.portalGuide: In **Network Watcher**, select **IP flow verify** (under Network diagnostic tools). Target: `{{vmName}}`, Protocol: `{{protocol}}`, Direction: **Outbound**, Local IP: (VM IP), Local port: `*`, Remote IP: `{{targetIp}}`, Remote port: `{{targetPort}}` > click **Check**. Observe whether the result is **Access Allowed** or **Access Denied**, and view the matching NSG security rule.
steps.cliCommand:
VM_NIC_ID=$(az vm show --name {{vmName}} --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} --query 'networkProfile.networkInterfaces[0].id' -o tsv)

az network watcher test-ip-flow \
  --vm {{vmName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --direction Outbound \
  --protocol {{protocol}} \
  --local 10.0.0.4:* \
  --remote {{targetIp}}:{{targetPort}}

steps.title: Run Next Hop Analysis for Route Diagnostics
steps.portalGuide: In **Network Watcher**, select **Next hop** (under Network diagnostic tools). Target: `{{vmName}}`, Source IP: (VM IP), Destination IP: `{{targetIp}}` > click **Next hop**. Inspect whether the next hop is **Internet**, **VirtualAppliance**, or **VirtualNetwork**.
steps.cliCommand:
az network watcher show-next-hop \
  --vm {{vmName}} \
  --resource-group {{resourceGroup}} \
  --source-ip 10.0.0.4 \
  --dest-ip {{targetIp}}
